official.description_text:
Doctoral student in nonlinear optical materials
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
Project description
Third-cycle subject:
Applied Physics
We are looking for a doctoral student who wants to develop the next generation of reconfigurable photonic platforms for quantum technologies. The project combines nonlinear optics, ferroelectric materials, micro-/nanofabrication, and quantum photonics, with a focus on programmable ferroelectric-based components. You will join a dynamic and international research group at KTH Applied Physics, where experimental research, materials development, and new photonic concepts come together. You will work in close collaboration with leading research groups in materials science and quantum technology, both at KTH and internationally. We are looking for candidates with a background in engineering physics, physics, photonics, quantum technology, or a related field.
Supervision:
Carlota Canalias is proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission.
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach and
analyze and work with complex issues.
It is considered a merit if you have documented knowledge and experience in one or more of the following areas: generation and characterization of squeezed light, ferroelectricity, and the fabrication, structuring, and use of ferroelectric crystals for nonlinear optical applications. Experience in experimental work in quantum optics, nonlinear optics, or photonic device fabrication is also considered a merit.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with
many employee benefits
and monthly salary according to
KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement
. Read more about

To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include the following elements:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled
language requirements (see above)
. Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages.Copies of originals must be
certified
.
CV including your relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (Maximum 2 pages long)
Representative publications or technical reports. For longer documents, please provide a summary (abstract) and a web link to the full text.
Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
Other information
For

If this applies to the specific position, a security clearance will be conducted for the applicant in accordance with the same law with the applicant's consent. In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.
We firmly decline all contact with staffing and recruitment agencies and job ad salespersons.

ai.summary: KTH doctoral position in reconfigurable photonic platforms combining nonlinear optics, ferroelectric materials, micro-/nanofabrication, and quantum photonics for quantum technologies. Experimental materials and device development.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. Position is in quantum photonics, ferroelectric materials, and photonic device fabrication—pure physics and materials science. Researcher's domain is HCI, immersive learning, and spatial cognition.

methodological_fit.rationale: No methodological transfer. Posting requires experimental work in nonlinear optics, ferroelectric crystal fabrication, and quantum photonics characterisation. Researcher's strengths are software development, UX design, and user studies—entirely orthogonal skill sets.

growth_value.rationale: Position offers no capability development relevant to human-centred XR or immersive systems. Complete domain retraining required with no strategic return to target identity.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH reputation and Stockholm location are positives. Supervisor expertise in quantum photonics is strong. However, quantum technology research trajectory diverges entirely from human-centred design and learning sciences.

eligibility_flags: Posting expects background in engineering physics, physics, photonics, quantum technology, or related field. Researcher's Creative Multimedia Master's is not credible background.
Merits include documented experience in squeezed light generation, ferroelectricity, ferroelectric crystal fabrication, or quantum optics. Researcher has none.
Experimental work in quantum optics/photonics listed as merit; researcher has zero experience in this domain.
risks: Core research is pure quantum photonics—outside poor-fit exclusion list but fundamentally incompatible with human-centred XR trajectory.
Researcher lacks all prerequisite physics and materials science background.
No clear pathway from this research direction to target identity.
